item.title: Gunmen kill 16, injure four in overnight attack on Plateau community
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos No fewer than 16 persons, including women, youths and children, have been killed after gunmen stormed Tafi Gana community, a hamlet of Kyie Ihwien, near Jebbu Miango in Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State. The attack, according to the Irigwe Development Association (IDA), occurred at about 11:30pm on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, leaving four other persons injured and throwing the community into confusion, fear and panic. The association, in a statement signed by its Public Relations Officer, Sam Jugo, and made available to newsmen in Jos on Thursday, said, “The attackers wielded assault rifles and other dangerous weapons.” “They stormed the community and started shooting sporadically.” It added, “By dawn of Thursday, November 26, 2026, about 16 persons lay dead, while four other survivors were rushed to unknown medical facilities with various degrees of injuries.” The association gave the names of those killed as Moses Oko, 70; Maingwa Zere Rangya, 60; Danladi Ishaku, 45; Luka Danladi, 21; Elisha Luka, 18; David Danladi, 10; Ishaya Goslow, 18; Lami Danladi, 30; Isi Ishaku, 18; Zhime Ngaza, 75; ThankGod Danladi, 18; Gideon Joseph, 25; Ladi Abba, 65; Ruth Istifanus, 20; Mary Keyi, 18; and Lazarus Musa, 13. The statement quoted the traditional ruler of the area, Nggwe Gado Dama, as confirming the incident, adding that the matter had been reported to security agencies. It said, “The matter had been reported to security operatives who were, as at press time, at the scene of the attack.” The association condemned the killings and appealed to residents to remain calm and avoid taking the law into their hands. It said, “The IDA appeals to all natives not to take laws into their hands but allow the security agencies to do the needful to dispense justice to the slain.” The association expressed condolences to the bereaved families and the entire Irigwe nation, praying for the repose of the souls of the victims and God’s comfort for their immediate families. item.title: Mr Latin hands over TAMPAN presidency after eight years
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nollywood actor, Bolaji Amusan, popularly known as Mr Latin, has stepped down as president of the Theatre Arts and Motion Pictures Practitioners Association of Nigeria (TAMPAN) after eight years in office. Amusan handed over the association’s leadership to his successor, Ajala Jalingo, at a transition ceremony, announcing the development in a post on his Instagram page on Wednesday. Sharing a video of the handover, the actor described the occasion as the end of his eight year tenure as the association’s Global President. “Today, I officially handed over the TAMPAN flag to my successor, @ajala_jalingo, bringing my eight-year tenure as Global President to a close,” he wrote. Amusan, who became president in December 2018 following the resignation of his predecessor, Dele Odule, was re-elected unopposed in December 2022 for another four-year term. Although he has left the presidency, the actor will remain involved in the association as a member of its Board of Trustees. “I bow out with gratitude, honour and fulfilment, while embracing a new responsibility as a distinguished member of the prestigious Board of Trustees (BOT) of TAMPAN,” he added. He also expressed confidence in the association’s future under Jalingo’s leadership, saying the change in administration would not affect its commitment to service and development. “Leadership may change, but commitment to service and the growth of TAMPAN remains unwavering,” Amusan said. TAMPAN represents theatre and film practitioners across Nigeria, particularly those in the Yoruba movie industry. The association works to promote members’ interests and welfare, as well as the development of the entertainment sector. Amusan began his acting career in 1988 and is known for his comic roles in Yoruba films. He has also worked as a filmmaker and producer. item.title: Mourners Mark Hong Kong Fire Anniversary, Authorities Warn Against ‘Disorder’
item.description: A stream of mourners laid flowers Thursday at the site of a horrific fire that ripped through a Hong Kong apartment complex and killed 168 people a year ago, with authorities warning against “acts of disorder”. The world’s deadliest residential building blaze since 1980 began on the afternoon of November 26, 2025 and raged for two days, gutting seven of Wang Fuk Court’s eight high-rise buildings that were home to some 4,600 people. Authorities in the Chinese territory — where Beijing has cracked down on dissent — appear wary of commemorations taking on a political tone and plan no official memorial. Police on Thursday kept a low profile as mourners laid hundreds of bouquets at a small park beneath the charred shells of the ruined buildings. They included former residents who stood on the same spot a year ago desperately waiting for news of their loved ones. “Families are torn apart, and people died,” said Koey Tam, a housewife and former resident in her 40s who lost her home, adding that they “can never be compensated with a new flat and a huge sum of money”. Smoke rises from apartments after a major fire swept through several blocks at the Wang Fuk Court residential estate in Hong Kong’s Tai Po district on November 27, 2025. (Photo by DALE DE LA REY / AFP) The government was “a bit cold” to hold no official memorials, she added. “What can a memorial event possibly affect?” Grace Chan, 69, expressed her frustration at what she called people’s “self-censorship”, telling reporters that “at first, I thought they’d given us a large space” to pay respects to the victims. “Too many Hongkongers remain silent,” she said, as she left a single chrysanthemum at the site. Former resident Dorz Cheung told AFP that he still felt “very, very, very angry” about the government’s response to oversights exposed in the tragedy. “There are still so many emotions… anger, deep sadness, they’re all around.” ‘Seeking Accountability’ A mourner brings flowers to Wang Fu Court in Hong Kong on November 26, 2026, the site of a horrific fire that ripped through seven apartment blocks and killed 168 people a year before. (Photo by Peter PARKS / AFP) The blaze was Hong Kong’s worst disaster in more than seven decades, and a shock to the 7.5 million residents of one of Asia’s safest cities. The city’s number two official Eric Chan said the government will offer help to “lawful” memorial events, but warned against “acts of disorder”. The Chinese government’s Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office spoke this week against attempts to “cause chaos” under the guise of commemorations. According to media reports, some local journalists have faced internal pressure when covering the fire, including to shelve programmes originally scheduled to go on air. A government spokesperson told AFP that as long as it is “within the law”, there are “no restrictions on the freedom to comment and criticise government policies for media outlets”. item.title: Musk says will give two SpaceX shares to ‘every child in America’
item.description: Tech billionaire Elon Musk said Wednesday he would give every child in the United States two shares in his SpaceX rocket company, doubling an offer he made last month. “Every child in America will receive two SpaceX shares, one from the company and one from me personally,” Musk said in a post on X, the social media platform he also owns. The world’s richest person said the share from SpaceX would be transferred next month, while the share from him personally would be transferred in June next year. He did not provide any further details about how the scheme would work. “I recommend holding on to your shares,” Musk said, claiming that SpaceX could “be worth about a million times the current global economy” if it “succeeds in making life multiplanetary and harnessing even a millionth of the Sun’s energy.” “These are obviously absurdly difficult goals, but there is a path to achieving them,” he said. In October, Musk promised that every child in the US would receive one SpaceX share, adding that it would be “the first of many.” There are around 73 million people under the age of 18 in the country, according to 2024 data from the Census Bureau. The closing price of one SpaceX share was $127.44 on Wednesday, meaning Musk’s gift would be worth a combined $18.6 billion. SpaceX made its stock market debut in June, raising about $85.7 billion. The company’s Starship megarocket reached orbit for the first time in September, a milestone for the spacecraft central to Musk’s ambition to colonize Mars. item.title: The Deposit Takes Seconds but Why Does the Withdrawal Take Days
item.description: When online, especially depositing money can feel almost effortless. When playing games online, a player chooses a payment method, enters their required details and they often see the funds appear in their account within a matter of seconds. When the time comes when the player wants to withdraw their money , it can be a very different experience. The request may remain pending for hours before additional processing and banking delays extend the wait across several days. That contrast naturally causes frustration. If a platform can accept money instantly, why can it not return money at the same speed. The answer involves more than payment technology. Withdrawals move through security checks, internal approval processes, payment providers, and banking systems that deposits may not encounter in the same way. Deposits and Withdrawals Are Not Mirror Images A deposit is designed to confirm that funds are available and can be transferred successfully. Payment networks can authorize many card and digital wallet transactions almost immediately. Once authorization is received, the casino can credit the player’s balance, even if the complete financial settlement happens later. A withdrawal requires the platform to release funds from its own system. Before doing so, the operator may need to confirm the player’s identity, verify account ownership, review transaction history, and check whether promotional conditions have been satisfied. The payment must then be approved and sent through an eligible withdrawal method. This difference means that an instant deposit does not prove that an instant withdrawal is technically or operationally possible. However, it also does not excuse operators that create unnecessary obstacles or fail to communicate their procedures clearly. Verification Can Become the First Bottleneck Identity verification is one of the most common reasons for a delayed withdrawal. Casinos may request proof of identity, proof of address, or evidence showing that the payment method belongs to the account holder. These checks are intended to reduce fraud, prevent unauthorized payments, and meet financial compliance obligations. Problems arise when verification is delayed until a player asks to withdraw. Someone may have deposited and played without interruption, only to discover that documents are required before any winnings can be released. Uploading those documents takes minutes, but manual review may take considerably longer, particularly during weekends or periods of high demand. item.title: Trump, NATO chief urge Russia not to ‘expand’ Ukraine war
item.description: US President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte urged Russia not to “expand the war” in Ukraine, in a joint statement issued Wednesday after meeting in Florida. The “outstanding” and “very impactful” meeting focused on the wars in Ukraine and Iran, said the statement issued by the White House after the closed-door talks at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort. “We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible,” the statement added. The joint appeal by Trump and Rutte comes despite the US leader describing Russian President Vladimir Putin as “my friend” during a meeting in China last week. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has taken issue with Trump’s comments on Putin. “For us, he is a killer,” Zelensky told CNN. Rutte was asked about Trump’s comments in an interview with Fox News’ “Fox & Friends” on Wednesday. “What President Trump is doing, also in the meeting in Shenzhen, is testing Putin,” the NATO secretary general said. “How serious is he? Is he willing to come to the negotiating table? Is he willing to really engage in talks. “So let’s keep the pressure on. I think it is working, and we have to keep that going.” Trump, accused by critics of siding with Moscow over Kyiv, said following his meeting with Putin that the Russian leader wants to see the war end by “diplomatic means.” The Florida meeting comes as European nations have expressed a desire to join preliminary talks that have so far only included Ukraine, the United States and Russia. Rutte said any agreement is going to have to include security guarantees for Ukraine. “When the war ends, either with a peace deal, preferable, or if not possible, a long-term ceasefire, we need to make sure that Ukraine has the security guarantees going forward,” he said. “But the most important thing here,” Rutte added, “is that we have to make sure that Ukraine has what it needs to keep the fight going, being so successful and putting that maximum pressure on the Russians.” Trump and Rutte also discussed increasing defense spending, which the US president has pressed European powers to do, the joint statement said. The Florida talks also came as Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth is expected to announce in coming weeks a review of the US force presence in Europe. item.title: US targets Africa’s critical minerals to counter rivals
item.description: In 2026, the United States went on an economic offensive looking to access critical minerals across Africa in its race to compete with China for materials that are essential for new technologies and the energy transformation. Will 2027 deliver on these promises for African governments and will the new Democrat-controlled US Congress complicate US deals with investigations into their transparency? – Investments or promises? – American companies and consortiums this year announced large-scale mining investment projects through partnerships in Guinea, South Africa, Mozambique and Kenya. But it was the strategic partnership agreed in December 2025 with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) that illustrated Washington’s economic push to secure its supply of critical minerals and reduce dependence on China. China has had a long head-start. It began investing in the African mining sector in the 1990s. The deal stipulated that Kinshasa would identify a portfolio of mining assets on which American investors have a right of first offer. In return, the Congolese government secured diplomatic support from Washington on security in its volatile eastern region, rocked by violence by myriad armed groups for more than 30 years. Since then, the American company Virtus Minerals, in partnership with the Indian group Lloyds Metals&Energy, has announced the acquisition of Chemaf, a heavily indebted Congolese company specialising in copper and cobalt. Orion Critical Mineral Consortium is negotiating with the international group Glencore for a 40-percent stake in its Mutanda and Kamoto mines, which also produce copper and cobalt. – Transparency probes? – Kinshasa urged Washington this month to “move from signed agreements to actual investments”. But the Democrats’ triumph in the US midterm elections could complicate the implementation of the partnerships concluded by the Trump administration amid questions about their transparency. The Democrats have already announced plans to open investigations early next year into the conditions under which the Trump administration conducted the negotiations. “Nothing should change in 2027 regarding the partnership principle, because the supply of minerals is of strategic national interest to the United States,” a mining source in the DRC told AFP. “The industry received bipartisan assurances on this issue in the run-up to the elections,” the source added. “But the agreements could be subject to opportunistic scrutiny by the Democrats, which might slow their implementation,” the source said. – Local economic benefits? – Several African countries have clearly demonstrated their determination to draw economic benefits from the partnerships. Zimbabwe suspended exports of raw minerals in February, ahead of a total ban in 2027, saying it would require processing and transformation to take place in the country. item.title: How OBJ stopped Gaddafi’s AK-47 convoy at Abuja airport in 2006 – Fani-Kayode
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini, Ambassador Olufemi Fani-Kayode, has disclosed how former President Olusegun Obasanjo refused to let assassinated Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi’s delegation bring high-powered weapons into Abuja in 2006, a decision he said saved lives. Fani-Kayode, a former minister of aviation, gave the account in a Facebook post titled “20 Years Ago With Muammar Ghaddafi!” who had then arrived in Nigeria for the African and South American Heads of State Summit. He said he received the Libyan leader at the airport on Obasanjo’s behalf and was detailed to accompany him for four days. “He arrived at the airport with no less than approximately 200 bodyguards, all with sidearms, and at least 100 cars (which had been sent ahead and were parked at the airport) to convey him to Abuja. The boot of each of those cars was filled with AK-47s and all manner of sophisticated weapons,” he said. Fani-Kayode said the convoy was blocked at the gate by Nigerian security personnel and the military. He said Gaddafi, members of his delegation and even his bodyguards would be allowed in with their sidearms, but not the weapons in the boots of the vehicles. After three more failed attempts to leave, he said, the Libyan leader lost his temper. “Ghaddafi totally lost his temper, got out of his car and started walking under the burning sun, past the airport gate and towards Abuja saying that if the cars were not allowed in he would walk there instead. Every single one of his 200 bodyguards and delegation members walked behind him!” he said. He said he called Obasanjo, who was on his way to the airport to travel to Lagos, and told Gaddafi the President was coming to settle the matter himself. Gaddafi agreed to return to the airport. Fani-Kayode said Obasanjo greeted Gaddafi warmly, apologised for the blockage and promised that the gates would be opened. But as he left, the then President whispered an instruction to him. “As he walked past me he bent over and whispered into my ear that under no circumstances would Ghaddafi and his team be allowed in unless they complied with our request that they drop the AK 47’s from the boots of their cars and put them back on their plane,” he said. He said Gaddafi’s Minister of National Security and Head of Protocol had threatened to fly the Libyan leader home and boycott the entire conference if the weapons were not allowed in. The Libyan officials complied after what he described as a “hot encounter and harsh trading of words”. According to him, the weapons were returned to the plane, which Nigerian soldiers then surrounded to ensure they were not smuggled out later. item.title: 2027: ADC’s Babba Kaita Rallies Katsina Voters, Promises LG Autonomy, Anti-Corruption Drive
item.description: The Katsina State Governorship Candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) for the 2027 general elections, Senator Ahmad Babba Kaita, has described the forthcoming polls as a crucial battle that Nigerians must pursue with determination and collective strength. Senator Kaita made the declaration while continuing his campaign tour across the Funtua Zone, where he sought the support and confidence of voters ahead of the 2027 elections. Addressing supporters during the campaign engagements, the former federal lawmaker said only Nigerians who are directly affected by governance challenges can fully explain the difficulties facing the country, arguing that the electorate has the power to determine the direction of the nation through their votes. According to him, the growing enthusiasm witnessed during ADC campaigns, including those led by the party’s presidential candidate and former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, demonstrates Nigerians’ desire for a new political direction. Kaita said the reception accorded the ADC across the country, including Katsina State, shows that citizens are prepared to use the ballot box to pursue what he described as positive change. The ADC governorship candidate also disclosed that candidates of the party from the seven North-West states have agreed to implement a common development agenda focused on tackling insecurity, improving education, boosting agriculture, strengthening healthcare delivery, expanding economic opportunities and promoting social development. On his plans for Katsina State, Senator Kaita reiterated his commitment to granting full autonomy to local government areas within his first six months in office if elected. He said his administration would conduct local government elections within the first three months, describing grassroots governance as a critical foundation for effective development. However, Kaita warned that local government administrations and other government institutions under his leadership would be subjected to strict monitoring to prevent abuse and mismanagement of public resources. “We will establish a state-owned Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) that will ensure the judicious management of our resources for the benefit of the people of Katsina State,” he assured. In a statement issued by the Spokesman of Kaita, the ADC campaign train is currently touring the 11 local government areas of Funtua Zone, attracting large crowds of supporters across towns and villages. The statement said residents, including youths, women and community leaders, have continued to welcome the campaign team with prayers, endorsements and assurances of support as the party intensifies its mobilisation ahead of the 2027 elections. item.title: New York Postpones Thanksgiving Day Parade Over Major Storm
item.description: New York postponed the iconic Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday over fears of extreme weather, a first in the event’s 100-year history, as a major storm gathers steam on the US East Coast. The brewing “nor’easter” threatens to disrupt plans for millions of people hitting the road and flying around the Thursday holiday, one of the country’s busiest travel seasons. “With severe weather expected on Thanksgiving Day, and out of an abundance of caution, in partnership with the City the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will be postponed,” Macy’s told AFP in a statement. A balloon of Buckaroo Bob The Minion rests under protective netting during the inflation of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade balloons on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, on the eve of the parade in New York City, on November 25, 2026. Photo by TIMOTHY A. CLARY / AFP The date change has prompted questions about the thousands of parade participants, including musicians and technical staff, who had made arrangements for a Thursday parade. “Our team is now working through the complex operational logistics required to bring the Parade to life on Saturday,” the company said. The annual parade sees brightly colored balloons travel some 2.5 miles (four kilometers) from Midtown Manhattan to Macy’s Herald Square flagship store on 34th Street. Millions of people typically gather to catch a glimpse of the festivities. It is the first time in its history that it has been postponed, The New York Post reported. ‘Heartbroken’ New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks during the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed press conference on November 25, 2026 in New York City. Manoli Figetakis/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by Manoli Figetakis / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) “This will be a heavy storm. We are expecting sustained winds between 30 and 40 miles per hour, with gusts as high as 60 to 65 miles per hour possible,” Mayor Zohran Mamdani told a safety briefing Wednesday. “The National Weather Service has issued a high wind warning as well as a coastal flood warning. “Winds will be strong enough (Thursday) to down tree limbs and power lines.” The worst of the storm will strike later Thursday when strong winds, heavy rain and the evening high tide will overlap, the city warned in a travel advisory. Organizers would have been only too aware of the gusting winds that wrecked the parade in 1997. Workers prepare a balloon under protective netting during the inflation of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade balloons on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, on the eve of the parade in New York City, on November 25, 2026. Photo by TIMOTHY A. CLARY / AFP Volunteers struggled but failed to keep a tight rein on ropes which constantly threatened to slam into onlookers. item.title: Protesters, FIFA boss, Democrat, spy: People who helped define 2026
item.description: Of the many people who made their mark on 2026, five in particular stand out — from an alleged Chinese spy to FIFA’s troubled president and a Madrid pensioner who became the face of Spain’s housing protests. – Alice Huang – She’s the woman at the heart of the international espionage scandal whose ripple effects are still emerging. Suspected of spying for Beijing, Alice Huang flew under the radar until the explosive revelation of her affair with the chief of US chip giant Nvidia, Jensen Huang. The outcry saw him resign, before being sensationally reinstated just days later after the intervention of US President Donald Trump. Alice Huang — no relation to the leather jacket-clad Jensen — is a former director of Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud computing company under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese tech firms obtain Nvidia AI chips in violation of US export controls. China denies the spying allegations. Alice Huang has not been seen since the scandal erupted. Details on her life are murky, but the Chinese citizen with a Hong Kong passport was filmed at a Taipei party in 2025 wearing a pink dress as she kissed Jensen Huang on the cheek. His departure on November 12 tanked Nvidia’s market value, sparking infighting within the Trump administration over what officials knew, and raising the spectre of trade clashes with China as the US tightens export controls of advanced AI chips. Nvidia’s shares rose 30 percent after the tech giant announced on November 23 that it had reinstated Huang, with Trump saying he had spoken to the board “directly”, igniting a political backlash and leaving many questions unanswered. – Gianni Infantino – FIFA President Gianni Infantino oversaw a highly successful World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico, even brushing off a controversial episode when USA forward Folarin Balogun had his red card suspended following a direct appeal by Trump. But football is a game of highs and lows, and within weeks Infantino faced calls to stand down over plans to sell stakes in World Cup commercial rights to a company run by the brother of Trump’s son-in-law. The proposal was hastily dropped following opposition led by European confederation UEFA, leaving Infantino’s re-election plans in March 2027 in peril. French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo was UEFA’s late choice as candidate. But he and veteran Japanese official Kozo Tashima face an uphill task to dislodge Infantino, who has been backed by the Asian, African and South American football federations. – Abdul El-Sayed – Democrat Abdul El-Sayed became the first Muslim elected to the US Senate following a stunning victory in the race for the Michigan seat during November’s midterm elections. “Michigan, we did it!” El-Sayed said of his win, one of many on a seismic night for his party. item.title: US lists 63 professions eligible for 3-year work visa
item.description: The US has outlined 63 professional categories whose qualified practitioners can apply for a temporary work visa allowing them to take up employment in the country for up to three years. The arrangement, known as the Trade National (TN) visa, is available exclusively to citizens of Canada and Mexico under the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA). The TN visa allows eligible professionals from the two neighbouring countries to work for US employers in specified occupations, provided they meet the educational, professional and employment requirements attached to their chosen fields. According to the US Department of State, applicants must be citizens of either Canada or Mexico, have a profession recognised under the USMCA list, secure a prearranged job with a US employer and possess the qualifications required for the position. The list covers several professional sectors, including healthcare, engineering, science, education, accounting and other specialised occupations. Some of the professions recognised under the arrangement include accountants, architects, engineers, lawyers, pharmacists, registered nurses, dentists, veterinarians, economists, mathematicians, scientists, university lecturers and computer systems analysts. Other eligible occupations include agriculturalists, biologists, chemists, geologists, meteorologists, psychologists, social workers, urban planners and technical publications writers. However, appearing on the list does not automatically guarantee approval, as applicants must demonstrate that they satisfy the specific educational or professional requirements for their occupations. Most of the listed professions require a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent, although some categories permit alternative qualifications or professional credentials. The US government also requires applicants to provide details of their proposed employment, including their job responsibilities, expected duration of stay, qualifications and remuneration arrangements. Under Section 214.6 of Title 8 of the US Code of Federal Regulations, successful TN applicants can be admitted into the country for a period not exceeding three years. The classification can also be extended, subject to the applicant continuing to meet the relevant requirements. The application process differs slightly between the two eligible nationalities. Canadian citizens can generally apply for TN status at a US port of entry or designated pre-clearance facility without first obtaining a TN visa from a US embassy. Mexican citizens, however, must obtain a TN nonimmigrant visa from a US embassy or consulate before seeking admission into the country. The arrangement was originally introduced under the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), which came into force in 1994. It was retained when the USMCA replaced NAFTA on July 1, 2020. item.title: ‘We will find a way to win’ insists Pochettino after rocky Man Utd start
item.description: New Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino insisted his team would find a way to win games after a tricky start to life at the helm of the Red Devils. United were held to a chaotic 2-2 Champions League draw at Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday, after a 4-0 thrashing by rivals Liverpool in his first match on Sunday. Man United, 19th in the Premier League, were upset with several refereeing decisions across both matches, but Pochettino said his team had to take responsibility for their situation. “I’m happy to be here,” said Pochettino, when asked about the various decisions that had gone against his team in his first week in charge. “We are here to take responsibility… we are going for sure to improve and to put that team in the place that, because of their history, we deserve to be. “Nothing is easy but we have the energy and I think we have the capacity, and most importantly the players and the power and the energy from our fans that is massive and I think united, all together, I think we will find a way to perform and win games.” United had two goals controversially ruled out against Sporting, but might have won the game were it not for a mistake from goalkeeper Senne Lammens. The Belgian dropped the ball for Colombian striker Luis Suarez to score his second goal of the night, cancelling out Bruno Fernandes’s double against his old side. Lammens also saved a Suarez penalty and then gave away a second penalty, this time scored by the striker. “This type of thing happens, that is football,” said Pochettino. “Football is about making mistakes — I’m going to support always my player if something happens.” The Argentine said Man United’s defenders might have done better to help protect Lammens before he spilled the ball. “When you are a ‘keeper, it’s not easy, that ball. And always you need help from your teammates,” added Pochettino. “But of course, we need to accept, we accept the challenge and we are here to try to improve in all the small details that for sure we will improve.” The post ‘We will find a way to win’ insists Pochettino after rocky Man Utd start appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Rewane projects 4.5% growth, urges investors to rethink strategies
item.description: By Onome Onyeme The Chief Executive Officer of Financial Derivatives Company, Bismarck Rewane, has projected Nigeria’s economic growth at between 4.3 and 4.5 per cent in 2027, urging investors to rethink traditional investment strategies and embrace emerging opportunities. Speaking at the 23rd edition of the Alpha Morgan Economic Review, held virtually yesterday, Rewane said changing economic realities, technological innovation and evolving business models were reshaping investment decisions globally. “The rules of the past are no longer the rules of the present, definitely not the rules of the future,” he said, urging investors to embrace innovation, research and emerging industries rather than rely on past market performance. Rewane, who examined global economic developments and Nigeria’s investment outlook, said businesses and investors that failed to adapt to changing realities risked losing relevance. He cited the evolution of global businesses, including Apple, as examples of how innovation and leadership could determine corporate fortunes, stressing that past success was no guarantee of future dominance. Rewane observed increasing participation in the capital market, with more companies raising funds through the market rather than relying solely on commercial bank loans. However, he warned of possible property market bubble risks, particularly amid the rapid expansion of construction and property investments in Lagos. Rewane projected that some companies could record revenue growth of between 25 and 40 per cent, driven by capital investment, expansion and increased operations across Africa. He also projected the Naira to trade between N1,500 and N1,600 per dollar in 2027, while anticipating an end to global interest rate increases. He clarified that the projections represented his personal assessment of economic developments. item.title: Five things to expect in 2027
item.description: Things are set to heat up in 2027. From rising temperatures to Democratic control of the US Congress to another total solar eclipse, here are five events to look out for in the coming year. El Nino in a hotter world With an El Nino cycle among the strongest ever observed, 2027 could break new global temperature records. El Nino is a naturally occurring weather phenomenon that emerges from the Pacific approximately every two to seven years. It shifts global rain patterns and brings higher temperatures to much of the planet, exacerbating rising temperatures caused by climate change. This year’s El Nino has already impacted maize in central America, fishery catches in Peru and sugar and rice production in Southeast Asia. But for harvests in some regions and food price spikes, “the worst is probably yet to come,” according to Kaveh Zahedi, of the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization. And these impacts will hit as farmers are already struggling with higher prices linked to the war in Iran, and with international aid reduced around the world. Democrats and Trump The Democratic takeover of both chambers of the US Congress in January promises to transform the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term, giving his opponents powerful tools to challenge his agenda — but not a free hand to impose their own. After their sweeping November midterm victory, Democrats plan an early push to ease living costs, including restoring Affordable Care Act insurance subsidies, reversing cuts to health care and rolling back Trump’s tariffs. They also want to end the war in Iran, which has driven up fuel prices. Hakeem Jeffries, poised to become the first black House speaker, will oversee a majority able to put Democratic bills to a vote, shape federal spending and use budget negotiations to press for concessions. Perhaps the more immediate impact will come from congressional investigations. Democratic-led committees can subpoena officials and demand documents on alleged corruption, Trump’s family business dealings, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war. Such scrutiny could trigger lengthy court battles. Democrats could also pursue a third impeachment of Trump, although removing him would require a two-thirds Senate majority — a formidable hurdle. In the Senate, Democrats can block Trump’s cabinet and judicial appointments, including any Supreme Court nominee. But most legislation needs 60 Senate votes to overcome procedural obstruction, and Trump can veto measures that reach his desk. Overriding him requires two-thirds majorities in both chambers. The result could be two years of subpoenas, spending standoffs and confrontation, punctuated by possible deals on shared priorities.
